text: Stored price levels in a std::map of std::list FIFOs with a hash map from order ID to list iterator for O(1) cancels, sustaining 1.26M events/sec over the full replay and a 1.2 µs per-update p99 on a separate 2M-event run
decisive_wording: B opens with "Sustained 1.26M events/sec ... 1.2 µs per-message p99" and then gives the mechanism as "keeping each price level as a FIFO queue (std::list) inside a std::map, with an order-ID hash map for O(1) cancels"; A opens with "Stored price levels in a std::map of std::list FIFOs with a hash map from order ID to list iterator"; C ends with "and a separate 2M-event run measured a 1.2 µs p99"
info: All three keep the throughput, the p99, the separate 2M-event run, std::map plus std::list FIFOs, and O(1) cancels. A and C say what the hash map points to (list iterator / list node), which is why cancels are O(1). B drops that detail and says only "order-ID hash map". B uses "per-message" where A says "per-update" and C gives no unit.

text: Traced an apparent 1.65x performance regression to the CPU frequency governor, not a code change, using perf counters and a do-nothing control book, then cut run-to-run variance from about 6% to 0.06% by pinning cores and fixing the clock
decisive_wording: "not a code change" and "do-nothing control book" (A) vs. "null control book" (B)
info: Both keep the 1.65x figure, the CPU frequency governor root cause, perf counters, the control book, the drop in variance from about 6% to 0.06%, core pinning, and the fixed clock. Only A says outright that the code was not at fault, and A calls the slowdown a "regression".
